subject: Measurement window defaults & ephemeral degradation carveout for Hosted API p50/p95
messages:
From: Paul Jenkins <paul.jenkins@finalpha.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Natalie Ortiz <natalie.ortiz@finalpha.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify measurement window + temporary carveouts for p50/p95 commitments

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo — the Hosted API performance looked promising. Before we proceed to procurement, we need clarity on two items that matter to our reliability and procurement team:

1) Measurement window defaults — Do you measure p50/p95 on a rolling 1-hour window, daily aggregation, or another scheme? We need something that aligns with our internal SLAs and audit traces.

2) Ephemeral degradations — our platform regularly deploys hourly canaries and runs short internal batch jobs that temporarily spike latency for a few minutes. Is there a documented carveout for these short-lived degradations (e.g., <5 minutes) so they don't count toward a monthly SLO breach? If so, what's the evidence required?

We have a target procurement date of Oct 15; if we can get a clear proposed addendum describing measurement rules and any transient-carveout logic, that will speed approvals.

Thanks,
Paul Jenkins
Director of Platform
FinAlpha


From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Paul Jenkins <paul.jenkins@finalpha.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify measurement window + temporary carveouts for p50/p95 commitments

Paul — thanks for the clear ask and for the quick follow-up. High level answer up front, then specifics and a proposed addendum we can attach to the contract.

High level: Redwood measures p50/p95 from a rolling 1-hour aggregation for the operational SLO dashboard, and we compute monthly rollups for contractual reporting. For contractual commitments we are proposing a month-level accounting based on weighted hourly windows with a transient-degradation carveout for short-lived events under defined conditions.

Proposed carveout (summary):
- Ephemeral events under 5 minutes by default qualify for auto-carveout if they meet two conditions: (a) they are observed as regional bursts affecting <10% of customer tokens during the event, and (b) the event is explained by an orchestrated activity (e.g., canary deploy, planned cache warm-up, or known maintenance) recorded in our incident/maintenance log.
- For unexplained short degradations, we require evidence (traces, k8s deployment timestamps, or load generator correlation) to apply the carveout.

Evidence package (what FinAlpha would need to provide or allow us to inspect):
- Deployment timestamps or maintenance windows (timestamped)
- Sample traces for a 10-minute window around the event (we'll accept minimal spans)
- Token-level request count demonstrating <10% impact during the event window

Next steps: Ben and Marissa — can you confirm that the proposed 5-minute auto-carveout rule is operationally safe for hosted multitenant capacity and provide the minimal evidence checklist we can add to the contract? Laura, can you draft the addendum language? I attached a quick template to start.

Paul — attaching "proposed-slo-addendum-v1.pdf" and the measurement checklist. If that looks right, we can produce a redline-friendly version for your procurement team.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposed-slo-addendum-v1.pdf, measurement-evidence-checklist.csv


From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Paul Jenkins <paul.jenkins@finalpha.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify measurement window + temporary carveouts for p50/p95 commitments

Thanks for the ping. Quick operational perspective and a couple of clarifications:

1) Measurement windows — our runtime emits per-request latency metrics with 1-second granularity and we maintain rolling 5m/15m/60m quantiles. For contractual reporting we bake hourly quantiles into a monthly rollup with weight proportional to token volume in each hour. Using rolling 1-hour windows for operational alerts (p95 crossing) and hourly buckets for contract-level reporting is consistent with what customers expect.

2) Carveout behavior — auto-carveout for events <5 minutes is acceptable but we should scope the triggers tightly:
   - The event must be visible in our region-specific ingress metrics (not global) and show a clear deployment or scaling activity in the same minute-range.
   - We should exclude events driven by sustained capacity saturation (even if <5 minutes) unless a capacity-side mitigation (fallback to alternate model/region) was attempted.

3) Evidence minimal set (ops-proposed):
   - Deployment/Canary job id + CI/CD timestamp (ISO)
   - Region-specific ingress qps and token counts for the 10-minute window
   - Per-shard GPU/memory utilization screenshot or CSV sample (1-minute granularity)
   - Optional: customer lightweight confirmation (email chain or ticket number) to speed review

4) Measurement nuance — we should call out a hard lower bound for carveout frequency: auto-carveouts should be capped at 3 events per calendar month to prevent repeated abuse. Additional carveouts may be considered under waiver with post-hoc evidence.

I think this is conservative and operationally safe for Hosted (multitenant). Happy to iterate on language.

- Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference


From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Paul Jenkins <paul.jenkins@finalpha.com>, Natalie Ortiz <natalie.ortiz@finalpha.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Oct 2026 14:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify measurement window + temporary carveouts for p50/p95 commitments

Paul / Natalie — thanks for the patience and for the specificity. We've updated the proposed addendum to reflect Ben's operational constraints and added the cap on auto-carveouts. Summary of agreed terms below — please reply if this tracks with FinAlpha and we will issue a redlineable addendum.

Agreed summary (proposed addendum highlights):
- Measurement: Contractual p50/p95 will be reported as token-weighted hourly bucketed quantiles aggregated over the billing month. Operational alerts use rolling 1-hour quantiles.
- Transient carveout: Events shorter than 5 minutes may be auto-excluded from monthly SLO accounting if both (1) they affect a single region and impact <10% of tokens, and (2) they are explained by an orchestrated activity (e.g., documented canary, planned maintenance, or cache warm-up) recorded in either the customer's maintenance log or our incident/maintenance log.
- Evidence: FinAlpha may provide deployment timestamps, regional ingress token counts, and a minimal trace sample; Redwood may require per-shard utilization samples if capacity saturation is suspected.
- Frequency cap: Auto-carveouts limited to 3 per calendar month; additional carveouts considered via waiver after joint review.
- Review SLA: Redwood will respond to carveout evidence submissions within 5 business days.

Attachments: proposed-slo-addendum-v1.pdf (updated), measurement-evidence-checklist.csv

If that matches, Paul — we'll prepare a redline and the HS record (HS-Record-DF-3219) and share the Drive link. Happy to hop on a 20-min call tomorrow if you want to walk the procurement team through the language.

Thanks,
